input.question: In contact sports when bodychecking an opponent, do you gain extra force by leaving your feet?
input.ground_truth: Being off the ground does not itself make you have extra force, but rather it is having a lot of force that tends to make you leave the ground. After all, when you are running or jumping you are pushing off of the ground, and the more powerfully you push, the further from the ground you tend to go. A bigger problem with being in the air is that you have no ability to stop yourself from moving in the direction you are moving, which means that you are at a much higher risk of a collision than if you are on the ground and still able to maneuver yourself.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: In contact sports when bodychecking an opponent, do you gain extra force by leaving your feet?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you’re playing on a playground slide. If you just stand on the slide, you won’t go very fast. But if you push off the ground with your feet before sliding, you go zooming down faster!

In contact sports, when you bodycheck (which is like bumping into someone to move them), if you jump or push off the ground with your feet before hitting them, you can move faster and hit harder. That’s because you use the power from your legs to give you a big boost. So yes, leaving your feet can help you use more force when you bodycheck!
